<explanation>
Below is a step-by-step breakdown of how to turn OuterTune’s files and README into a clear, accurate system design diagram. The goal is to show every major component, how they relate, and the technologies that glue them together.

1. Identify Project Type and Purpose  
   • This is a multi-module Android application (“app” module) that acts both as a YouTube Music client and a local audio player.  
   • Supporting libraries/modules:  
     – innertube: a YouTube Music client library  
     – kugou: a third-party lyrics/metadata provider  
     – lrclib: a local LRC parser library  
     – material-color-utilities: dynamic theming utilities  
     – prebuilt/taglib AAR: FFmpeg-based metadata extractor plugin  

2. Analyze the File Structure  
   • Top-level modules:  
     – app/ : Android Gradle module (Jetpack Compose UI, Room database, ExoPlayer services, DI, ViewModels)  
     – innertube/, kugou/, lrclib/, material-color-utilities/: Kotlin libraries for network calls, parsing, theming  
     – prebuilt/: external AAR for taglib  
   • app/src/main/java/com/dd3boh/outertune/: follows MVVM – UI screens → ViewModels → Repositories / Data Sources → Room DB or network  
   • Services: ExoDownloadService, MusicService, MediaLibrarySessionCallback  
   • DI entrypoint: AppModule.kt  
   • Configuration: build.gradle.kts, schemas (Room), AndroidManifest, assets (HTML & SVG), resources  

3. Extract Insights from README  
   • Features: YouTube sync (via innertube), local playback, multiple queues, synchronized lyrics, audio effects, Android Auto.  
   • External dependencies: InnerTune fork, ffMetadataEx plugin.  

4. Core Components for the Diagram  
   a. Frontend (Android app):  
      – UI Layer: Jetpack Compose screens/components  
      – Presentation Layer: ViewModels (one per screen)  
      – Domain/Data Layer: Repositories, Use-cases (inferred from ViewModels → DAO / network calls)  
      – Services:  
         * MusicService / MediaLibrarySessionCallback → exposes media session to UI/Android Auto  
         * ExoDownloadService → handles downloads & offline cache (HybridCacheDataSinkFactory)  
      – Database: Room (MusicDatabase + DAOs + Entities + Converters)  
      – Dependency Injection: Hilt / Dagger (AppModule)  
   b. Library Modules (all included as Gradle dependencies):  
      – innertube: YouTube Music API client → HTTP (JSON)  
      – kugou: lyrics API client → HTTP (JSON)  
      – lrclib: LRC file parser → local parsing  
      – material-color-utilities: dynamic theming  
      – prebuilt/taglib AAR: FFmpeg metadata extractor  
   c. External Services:  
      – YouTube Music (via innertube HTTP endpoints)  
      – KuGou Lyrics service (via kugou HTTP endpoints)  
      – Local file system (assets, media files)  

5. Relationships & Data Flows  
   – UI Components → invoke ViewModels  
   – ViewModels → call Repositories / Services via injected interfaces  
   – Repositories → decide between:  
     • Room DB (DAOs)  
     • Network client (innertube, kugou)  
     • File parser (lrclib, prebuilt taglib)  
   – Media playback chain:  
     UI Play Command → MusicService → ExoPlayer → Local cache &/or network stream → OS AudioTrack  
   – Lyrics retrieval chain:  
     UI → ViewModel → LyricsHelper → {innertube transcript API, kugou search} → LRC parser → UI  

6. Architectural Patterns & Principles  
   • MVVM (UI ↔ ViewModel ↔ Model)  
   • Layered architecture (Presentation / Domain / Data)  
   • Single source of truth (Room DB + offline cache)  
   • DI for loose coupling (AppModule → provides DAOs, network clients, services)  
   • Modular structure for reusability & testability  

7. Tailoring the Diagram for this Android App  
   • Show one big “Android App” container (app module) subdivided into:  
     – UI (Compose)  
     – ViewModels  
     – Data/Domain (Repositories, Use Cases)  
     – Services (MediaSession, Download)  
     – Database (Room)  
     – DI  
   • Surrounding library containers: innertube, kugou, lrclib, material-color-utilities, prebuilt/taglib  
   • External “cloud” icons for YouTube Music API & KuGou API  
   • Show Android OS components: Audio subsystem, Android Auto  

8. Diagramming Guidelines  
   – Labels: every box/shape must be clearly labeled (e.g., “MusicService”, “QueueDao”, “InnerTube HTTP Client”)  
   – Arrows: directional, annotated with protocol/interaction type (e.g., “HTTP JSON”, “Room query”, “Method call”)  
   – Color coding:  
     * Blue for UI/presentation  
     * Green for data/repos/services inside app  
     * Orange for external libraries  
     * Gray clouds for external web services  
     * Cylinder icon for Room database  
   – Shapes:  
     * Rounded rectangles for components/modules  
     * Cylinders for databases  
     * Clouds for external services  
     * Hexagons for third-party libraries  

9. Putting It All Together  
   • Start with a Container View (C4-style):  
     [Android App]  
       ├─ UI Layer (Compose)  
       ├─ ViewModels  
       ├─ Services (MusicService, ExoDownloadService)  
       ├─ Repositories / Data Sources  
       ├─ Room Database  
       └─ DI Module  
   • Show arrows from UI → ViewModels → Repositories → {Room, innertube, kugou, lrclib, taglib}  
   • Place library modules around the app container, arrows pointing inward (app “uses” library)  
   • Place YouTube Music & KuGou external clouds, arrows from innertube and kugou modules  
   • Show Android OS (Audio Subsystem, Android Auto) interacting with MusicService  

By following these steps—identifying modules, layering the app, mapping data flows, and using clear visual conventions—you will have a detailed, accurate system design diagram that captures OuterTune’s architecture end-to-end.
